messages:
eli: heads-up: ran long-doc holdout (news/articles) to validate chunked-embedding pipeline for argo-lite-int6. notable R@10 drop vs fp16 for long-doc queries (chunked). attaching quick paste.
eli: command:
```
./embed_longdoc_bench --model=argo-lite-int6 --holdout=longdocs_3k --chunk_len=512 --stride=256 --k=10 --quant=per-tensor
```

sam: paste numbers plz. small thread helps triage.
eli: table (avg 3 runs):
```
model           doc_type  R@1    R@5    R@10
argo-fp16       short     0.472  0.789  0.831
argo-int6       short     0.468  0.783  0.827
argo-fp16       long      0.401  0.742  0.786
argo-int6       long      0.385  0.698  0.712  <-- large R@10 drop
```

zoe: interesting that short docs unaffected. chunking + quant interaction maybe? did you aggregate chunk vectors differently?
eli: same aggregation (maxpool over chunk vectors), same whitening (PCA trained on mixed short+long sampled embeddings).

sam: could be that quant noise perturbs chunk embeddings more because chunks have higher variance (contextual density). any norm stats?
eli: pasted norms (L2 mean/std per doc type):
```
metric    model       doc_type  mean_norm  std_norm
emb_norm  argo-fp16   long      13.1       2.2
emb_norm  argo-int6   long      12.6       4.5  <-- heavier tail on int6
```

zoe: heavy tail again. also check top1-top2 cosine gap across aggregated vectors (per-doc). if quant occasionally flips chunk ordering, maxpool will pick wrong chunk.
eli: ran quick cos-gap calc: avg gap fp16_long=0.09, int6_long=0.02. supports chunk-order flips.

benchbot: queued two jobs: (A) try mean-pooling instead of max (run 6192468201), (B) per-channel quant for int6 (run 6192468202).

benchbot: run 6192468201 complete (mean-pool): argo-int6 long R@10=0.735 (improved), cos-gap mean=0.045.
benchbot: run 6192468202 complete (per-channel): argo-int6-perchan long R@10=0.779, cos-gap mean=0.082 (near fp16).

sam: per-channel + keep current max-pool seems to restore most of gap. but mean-pool also helps and is cheaper config-wise. tradeoff: mean-pool reduces peak recall for some head queries? did you check short docs?
eli: short docs: int6-perchan short R@10=0.825 (same). mean-pool short R@10=0.813 (down small).

zoe: recommendation: prefer per-channel quant for chunked long-doc flows. alternatively, if per-channel cost unacceptable, change aggregation to mean-pool for long-doc only. also add a test in onboarding that runs chunked long-doc holdout and reports per-doc cos-gap distribution and per-agg-method deltas.
sam: file a PR to update onboarding: (1) add long-doc holdout case, (2) prefer per-channel quant for chunked pipelines, (3) add canary rule: fail int6 if long-doc R@10 drops >0.03 vs fp16 or if avg cos-gap drops below 0.05.
eli: opening PR and ticket EMBED-ONB-3644 with artifacts and UMAP snapshots.

ops-bot: ticket EMBED-ONB-3644 created and assigned to eli. artifacts: /artifacts/6192468000/*

zoe: nice catch. chunking + aggregation is an extra axis for quant sensitivity we should add to docs.
sam: thanks team :thumbsup:
